newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain government studying tax cuts, simplification.
newsitem.headline: Spain government studying tax cuts, simplification.

text.p: Spain's government is studying a cut in personal income tax and a simplification of the tax system, a spokeswoman for tax authority Hacienda said on Wednesday.
No details or dates for the changes were made public.

"The idea is to reform the tax system, both simplifying and reducing personal income tax as well as revising certain tax deductions in other areas. But it's still very soon to be more concrete on this," the spokeswoman told Reuters.
"It's still very vague, but the idea is to cut income taxes, which in principle would be effective from next year," she added.
The spokesman said a committee had been formed to study changes in income tax and will produce a report.

Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato said in a radio interview on Tuesday that deductions in tax breaks on certain types of investment would make lower income taxes "possible in terms of (government) fiscal receipts."
